knowledge_point.title: Interpreting the Derivative of a Function

question.:question/problem: Consider a circle. Let $A$ denote the area and let $d$ denote the diameter. The diameter can vary. What is the best interpretation of ${A}^{′}(d)$?
question.:question/worked-solution:
The function $A(d)$ gives the area of the circle as a function of the diameter. So,

$$
{A}^{′}(d)=\frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}d}=\frac{\text{Instantaneous change in }A}{\text{Change in }d}.
$$

Therefore, ${A}^{′}(d)$ is the rate at which the area changes as the diameter changes.

:answer-field/choices.:answer/value: The rate at which the diameter changes as the area changes
The diameter of the circle
The rate at which the circumference changes as the diameter changes
The area of the circle
The rate at which the area changes as the diameter changes

The function $P(s)$ gives the perimeter of a square with side $s.$ So,

{P}^{′}(s)=\frac{\text{d}P}{\text{d}s}=\frac{\text{Change in }P}{\text{Change in }s}.
$$

Therefore, ${P}^{′}(s)$ is the rate at which the perimeter changes as each side changes.

question.:question/problem: Consider an ellipse such that its major axis $a$ can vary while its minor axis is fixed. What is the best interpretation of ${S}^{′}(a)$ if $S$ is the area enclosed by the ellipse?

$$
{S}^{′}(a)=\frac{\text{d}S}{\text{d}a}=\frac{\text{Change in }S}{\text{Change in }a}.
$$

Therefore, ${S}^{′}(a)$ is the rate at which the area changes as the major axis changes.
